text:
INVENTED SAMPLE PAPER FOR TESTING. Every name, number, date and place below is made up. It is not a real case.

FIRST INFORMATION REPORT (under section 154 Cr.P.C.)
Police Station: Exampleville City Police Station, District Sampleton. FIR No. 0214 of 2024. Date of report: 22.04.2024.
1. Offences: sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2. Complainant: Meera Vellacott, proprietor of M/s Vellacott Agencies, Market Road, Exampleville.
3. Accused named: Rohit Brindlewood, proprietor of M/s Brindlewood Traders, Canal Street, Exampleville.
4. Date and place of occurrence: on 10.02.2024 at the shop of the complainant, Market Road, Exampleville.
5. Brief facts: The complainant states that on 10.02.2024 the accused came to her shop and asked for goods worth Rs. 4,50,000 on credit, promising to pay within thirty days. The complainant says the accused told her that his own stock had been sold and that payment was certain. On the faith of that statement she handed over the goods against a delivery challan. The complainant says the accused did not pay. She says he gave her cheque no. 000123 dated 14.03.2024 drawn on Sample Bank Ltd, Exampleville Branch, and that the cheque came back unpaid. She says the accused had no intention of paying when he took the goods, and that he has since closed his shop and does not answer her calls.
6. The complainant states that she sent a written notice to the accused on 12.04.2024 and he did not reply.
7. Action taken: the report was registered at 6.40 p.m. on 22.04.2024 and given to Sub-Inspector A. Example for investigation.
Signature of the complainant: (invented)    Signature of the officer in charge: (invented)

text:
INVENTED SAMPLE PAPER FOR TESTING. Every name, number, date and place below is made up. It is not a real case.

EXTRACT FROM THE FINAL REPORT (CHARGESHEET) under section 173 Cr.P.C.
Exampleville City Police Station, FIR No. 0214 of 2024. Date of final report: 24.06.2024. Court: Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sampleton.
Accused: Rohit Brindlewood. Sections: 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
Summary of the investigation: The investigating officer recorded the statement of the complainant Meera Vellacott and of one witness, Karan Placeholder, who was working at the shop of the complainant. The accused Rohit Brindlewood was arrested on 27.06.2024 and produced before the Magistrate on 28.06.2024. The investigating officer states that the goods were handed over to the accused on 12.02.2024 against delivery challan number 88. The delivery challan was seized from the complainant. The cheque numbered 000123 dated 14.03.2024 and the return memo dated 20.03.2024 were also seized. The investigating officer states that the accused has closed his shop and was traced at his residence on 05.05.2024 and gave his statement, in which he denies that he ever took the goods.
Findings: The investigating officer finds that the dispute arises from a business transaction. The investigating officer states that a complaint under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 has also been filed by the complainant before the competent court. The investigating officer nevertheless says there is material to show that the accused made a false promise at the time of taking the goods.
Witnesses relied on: (1) Meera Vellacott; (2) Karan Placeholder. Documents relied on: delivery challan, cheque, return memo, legal notice dated 12.04.2024.
Submitted for the court's orders. Signature: (invented).

name: Bail order (invented sample)
text:
INVENTED SAMPLE PAPER FOR TESTING. Every name, number, date and place below is made up. It is not a real case.

IN THE COURT OF THE SESSIONS JUDGE, SAMPLETON
Bail Application No. 117 of 2024. State v. Rohit Brindlewood. FIR No. 0214 of 2024, Exampleville City Police Station.
Order dated 03.07.2024.
1. The applicant Rohit Brindlewood was arrested on 28.06.2024. This is an application for regular bail by the accused, who is in judicial custody since 28.06.2024 in connection with offences under sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the applicant and the learned Public Prosecutor.
3. The applicant says that the dispute is wholly civil, that the cheque transaction is being dealt with under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, that the charge sheet has been filed on 24.06.2024 and that custody is no longer needed for investigation.
4. The learned Public Prosecutor says that the applicant closed his shop and could not be traced for some days and that there is material of an intention to cheat at the time of taking the goods.
5. Having regard to the fact that the investigation is complete and the charge sheet has been filed, the offences are punishable with imprisonment of up to seven years, the amount alleged is Rs. 4,50,000 and the applicant has an address and has given his statement to the police, the court is satisfied that the applicant need not be kept in custody. The applicant is admitted to bail on furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000 with one surety of the like amount, on the condition that he shall attend the trial court on every date and shall not leave the district without leave of the court. The court relied on (2014) 8 SCC 273 on the need for reasons before arrest in offences punishable up to seven years.
6. The matter is listed on 05.08.2024 for framing of charges. The application is allowed. Nothing in this order is an expression on the merits of the case.
Sessions Judge: (invented).

PART 1 OF 2: SAMPLE BANK LTD, EXAMPLEVILLE BRANCH
CHEQUE RETURN MEMO
Date of memo: 20.03.2024
To: M/s Vellacott Agencies (payee), Market Road, Exampleville.
We return herewith the cheque described below, presented through your account on 18.03.2024.
Cheque number: 000123. Date of cheque: 14.03.2024. Amount: Rs. 4,50,000 (Rupees four lakh fifty thousand only).
Drawer: M/s Brindlewood Traders, account number ending 4471 (invented).
Reason for return: Funds insufficient.
This memo is issued under the rules of the bank. The cheque was presented within its period of validity.
Authorised signatory: (invented), Sample Bank Ltd.

 PART 2 OF 2: LEGAL NOTICE UNDER SECTION 138(b) OF THE NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS ACT, 1881
Date: 12.04.2024. Sent by registered post and by e-mail to the addressee.
To: M/s Brindlewood Traders, through its proprietor Rohit Brindlewood, Canal Street, Exampleville.
From: M/s Vellacott Agencies, through its proprietor Meera Vellacott, Market Road, Exampleville.
1. Our client supplied you goods worth Rs. 4,50,000 on 10.02.2024 against delivery challan number 88 and you promised to pay within thirty days.
2. In part discharge of that liability you issued cheque no. 000123 dated 14.03.2024 for Rs. 4,50,000 drawn on Sample Bank Ltd, Exampleville Branch.
3. Our client presented the cheque on 18.03.2024. It was returned unpaid on 20.03.2024 with the remark "Funds insufficient". Our client received the bank's information of dishonour on 21.03.2024. A copy of the return memo is enclosed.
4. We therefore call upon you to pay Rs. 4,50,000 within fifteen days of the receipt of this notice, failing which our client will file a complaint against you under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 and take other action in law.
Advocate for the sender: (invented). Postal receipt number 5521 dated 12.04.2024 (invented). The notice was delivered to the addressee on 15.04.2024, as the postal tracking shows.
